items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: Louis had a nephew who had a problem

ctx.x: Well it’s got to be something about the music because the people I’ve met that are associated with jazz have just been the classiest group, so on that note—

That’s for sure. You’re right. Well we know that because we have music therapy in the hospital named for Louis and we know what it’s done. Because Louis had a nephew who had a problem and he put him in a mental institution after nobody in the family could take care of him anymore. And the boy was, well he was a man of 32 and he was not acting properly and when Louis came to visit him he knew one thing, that Clarence didn’t have any music where he was, where he had always been in an atmosphere of music. So he…
That’s terrific. Well thanks to both of you for the important work you do. And it’s really uplifting to know that there’s support like this going on.
